_note: The third survey of Smetlede's centre (31 Oct 2026): the houses round the church square and along Smetlededorp to the school, for tools/town/town.py. Plans from the GRB outlines and the laser scan's roof parts (data/neighbours.json, by index in `grb`); walls, openings, roofs and colours read off Street View (August 2026 where the car passed, else April 2023 or older) and the orthophoto. Positions in the model (x, z in metres), colours as seen (sRGB); no addresses, names, signs or lettering. A volume: four corners p0..p3, p0-p1 along the ridge (the low side of a shed roof); faces by edge (0: p0-p1, 1: p1-p2, 2: p2-p3, 3: p3-p0); rows of openings per storey from the ground up (w window, W wide window, n narrow, o small, a arched, d door, D double door, g/G garage door, s shop window, c carport bay, _ blank pier; a number after the letter is its width in m), spread evenly with `margin` at the ends, or `at` [s along the face, token@storey].

houses._ref: The long low house on the square's west side: painted brick in cream over a brownish-pink painted plinth, brown shutters, small-paned white windows, orange clay tiles with three chimneys; its gable end on the square in bare red brick; a lower brick wing behind.
The brick barn at the long house's end: red brick, orange clay tiles, a wide olive-green door on the street, a blank gable on the parking with wall anchors.

The corner house on the square's east side: painted white brick on a grey plinth, a shop window and glazed double door in black frames on the square, two garage doors, wide upper windows with steel guards, a hipped slate-grey roof with three roof windows.
A narrow red-brown brick house next to the corner house: a door and window under two windows, white frames, anthracite tiles.
Painted white brick with blue surrounds round the windows and a yellow garage door, white frames, anthracite tiles; flat-roofed backs.

The renovated house across the street from the corner shop: smooth white render on an anthracite plinth, black frames, a dark grey garage door, three roof windows in anthracite tiles; its gable to the square with two small windows and two air-conditioning units.
Grey-beige painted render, dark brown frames, door and garage door; a lower white annex with a brown garage door; anthracite tiles.
Red-brown brick, two storeys under orange clay tiles with a long slope to the back, white frames.

The small painted house next to the portal's gap: off-white paint with sandstone-coloured surrounds, iron wall anchors, white frames, a door with a fanlight, dark tiles; its side to the gap with a small window.
Two yellow brick houses in a row: wide ground-floor windows and white doors, brown frames, dark grey plinths, anthracite tiles; a long flat-roofed hall behind.
Beige painted render with arched windows in white frames, decorative wall anchors, a white sectional garage door, a blue-stone plinth, dark tiles and a brick chimney.

The new block of flats (newer than the laser scan, so heights from the photos): a red-brick ground floor with open carport bays and a glazed entrance, two storeys of white render with wide black-framed windows, a set-back top floor and a roof terrace behind a glass railing.

The chip shop by the school behind its forecourt: white horizontal boards on a grey plinth, a counter under a dark sign band with a green light along its edges (no lettering), closed by a grey roller shutter between aluminium posts, a framed poster case left blank, a cream annex under a lean-to roof; a low bench and a bistro table at the counter.

The café by the church tower (a Street View photo of April 2023 from the owner): a narrow two-storey house of red-orange brick whose front is a crow-stepped gable, four steps a side and a flat top; courses of cream brick at the gable's foot and round the sign board, two lozenges of light brick beside the upper window; that window in olive-green frames with a transom, net curtains, a light stone sill and lintel; below, a white panelled door with a sunburst fanlight in a light brick surround and a step, and a wide window behind a white roller shutter; a blue-stone plinth; a white sign board between the floors with a plain red panel and the café's name. Roof and sides as the laser scan and an older photo from Kerkhofstraat show them: grey tiles, a rendered gable at the back with a chimney.

The low white house between the café and the church: painted brick, orange clay tiles, a green garage door and door on Kerkhofstraat, a small window in its gable by the café with the café's hanging sign.

On the lane past the square's north-east corner (April 2023): a low red brick cottage with its eaves along the lane, three windows with net curtains, dark pantiles and a roof window; in front of it a flat-roofed brick garage with a brown up-and-over door and a glass-block window.

On the lane opposite the café: an old two-storey red brick house with a wide dark timber double door under a row of small panes, a window over it patched in newer brick, stone sills, a letterbox; dark tiles; a long low back.

Next to it towards Kerkhofstraat: a newer two-storey red brick house, a dark door with glass strips, white roller shutters, a band of brick on edge at the first floor, a chimney on its gable to the street.

Kerkhofstraat past the fork: a red brick house with a steep gable to the street trimmed in white, a white door in a stone surround, a wide window with a flower box, three windows above and one in the gable; its side hung with dark slates.
At the fork towards the church: a detached two-storey house in light grey render on a dark plinth, white door, windows under white roller-shutter boxes, dark tiles; a low pale garage beside it.
Across Kerkhofstraat: a narrow two-storey house of yellow brick with a flat top, a window and a door below, one window above, a curved band of brick at the first floor.

West of the school on Smetlededorp: a three-storey block of red brick from the early twentieth century, segmental arches over the first floor's windows, a light stone band, two garage doors and two doors in stone surrounds, a square stair tower at its east end standing above the eaves, dark slates.

Further west: a two-storey red brick house under dark pantiles with a small gable over its middle, white frames under roller-shutter boxes, a door in a green frame, a wide brown timber barn door at its east end; a low white annex to the west; a flat-roofed workshop behind.

South side opposite: a detached house of brown-buff brick from the seventies, two storeys under a hipped roof of grey tiles with a roof window, white frames, a brown timber door, a white garage at its east end; flat-roofed rooms behind.
Behind the parking past the barn: a detached house of brown brick from the sixties under a hipped roof of dark tiles, a chimney, a balcony over the door, white frames; a wide flat-roofed wing behind.

Next to it: a pair of houses from the seventies in buff-brown brick, roofs of one slope rising to the back, wide windows below, a band of brown panels between the floors, brown frames and big chimneys; low rooms behind.

East of the square on Smetlededorp (older Street View): two houses of white glazed brick under dark tiles, a wide gable over the eastern one with a balcony of wrought iron, a glazed porch, white frames under roller-shutter boxes, a street lantern in front; lower rooms behind.
